answer: Each identity walks a five-milestone tundra trail, locking a 70-credit bond, passing ivory cairns. Each stop needs a signed, time-stamped nectar receipt and a 12-credit filing; auditors replay the log; a missing, late, or copied receipt burns it. A walker filing for many leaves identical timestamps, exposing the rented-trail ring. 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. Honest agents walk once, pay 60, keep the bond.
